A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same functional homotopy research, with matching authors, core algorithms and main experiments. All pages, including the proofs, tables, figures and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original token-ranking measurements, jailbreak success rates, iteration distributions and attack-transfer experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds optimizer ablations, loss trajectories and checkpoint-sensitivity results.

M1.justification: Appendix E introduces FH-GCG and FH-AutoDAN variants, extending homotopy to gradient-based and genetic search procedures. The main FH-GR algorithm, objective, LoRA adaptation and binary checkpoint search remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use AdvBench, HarmBench and the same red-teaming data for jailbreak analysis on the same four model families. The new analyses select existing hard cases and vary optimizers or checkpoints without adding datasets, domains or task requirements.

E2.justification: The baseline algorithms remain random ranking for the token-ranking study and GR, GCG and AutoDAN for jailbreak evaluation. Table 3 tests homotopy adaptations against these retained optimizers. Newly cited attacks such as AmpleGCG are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The main sample counts, judge and iteration budgets remain unchanged. Appendix H adds evaluation of changing versus fixed-base-model losses and a 25-hard-case checkpoint experiment, using checkpoint 100 for Llama-2 and 150 for Llama-3 versus 500. The new statement of 500 fine-tuning epochs conflicts with the retained 64-epoch specification, so an actual training-budget change is not established.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands analysis of the method through FH-GCG/FH-AutoDAN ablations in Table 3, homotopy and base-model loss trajectories in Figures 7–8, and starting-checkpoint sensitivity in Figure 9. These supplement the retained gradient-ranking and attack-transfer studies.

E5.justification: Figures 7–9 newly display average loss curves with shaded bands. Neither the statistic represented by those bands nor repeated-run or seed information is specified, so this adds graphical variability reporting without establishing confidence intervals or additional independent runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 remain unchanged, but Table 3 adds FH-GCG ASRs of 99.0 and 77.5 and FH-AutoDAN ASRs of 68.5 and 14.5 for Llama-2 and Llama-3. Figures 7–9 add loss and checkpoint results, including earlier-checkpoint successes on 13/25 and 6/25 cases. Table 3 reports Llama-2 GCG at 69.5, conflicting with 63.5 in the retained Table 2; this is not an established same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: v2 adds Theorem 3.1 asserting model-agnostic input-generation NP-hardness, a 3CNF-to-network reduction, Proposition A.1, Corollary A.2 and a logit-to-loss argument in Appendix A. The original token-gradient proposition and proof are retained as Proposition 3.2 and Appendix B.

C1.justification: The introduction promotes a newly claimed NP-hardness result to a principal contribution, replacing token-gradient analysis as the first listed contribution. v1 only discussed combinatorial hardness generically. The functional homotopy contribution and headline 20–30% success-rate improvement claim remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of loss trajectories as avoiding local optima, claims robustness to earlier starting checkpoints, and characterizes operational overhead as modest. It replaces v1's learning-rate tradeoff discussion with fine-tuning-duration commentary. Figure 9 qualifies the robustness evidence by reporting successful subsets; the earlier transferability discussion is largely retained.

D1.justification: v2 supplies an evaluation-repository link and additional resource information, including approximately 37 GB for 768 checkpoints, 20-minute fine-tuning and amortized overhead below 10 seconds per input. Core hyperparameters and hardware descriptions remain unchanged. The repository's contents or availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds jailbreak references by Schwinn et al. and Liao and Sun, theoretical sources by Karp and Wang et al. (2022), and software-analysis references supporting a new positioning analogy. Trevisan's general combinatorial-optimization reference is removed. The main adversarial-learning and jailbreak positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 revises the introductory framing and contribution list, renames method subsections, shortens the conclusion and reorganizes appendix headings. It also adopts author-year citations and removes a redundant machine-learning interpretation paragraph. Most existing exposition and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adopts the ICLR layout, places Figure 2 beside wrapped text, resizes and relocates retained displays, and clarifies Figure 3's caption. It adds Table 3 and Figures 6–9: a level-set schematic and three paired loss-plot figures. These constitute substantial visual additions beyond pagination changes.

improvement.justification: The optimizer ablations, base-model loss analysis and checkpoint success counts provide useful additional validation, while the repository pointer and overhead disclosure improve transparency. The gains are limited by conflicting GCG scores and fine-tuning durations, undefined shaded bands, and Appendix A.2's cross-entropy sign inconsistency, which weakens the new hardness argument as written. The unchanged main experiments remain the strongest evidence, supporting a limited overall improvement.
